findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS MySQL volume, snapshots and logs unencrypted, so any access to the underlying storage or a shared snapshot exposes the database contents in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance an internet-routable endpoint, exposing MySQL on port 3306 to untrusted networks and undermining the VPC-scoped security group boundary. The endpoint is also emitted as a Terraform output.

The master user is the predictable default 'admin' and the password comes from a plain (non-sensitive) Terraform variable that is stored in cleartext in state and interpolated into EC2 user data. Combined with public accessibility this invites credential guessing and brute force against a known account.

findings.issue_category: no IAM auth or audit logging
findings.description: iam_database_authentication_enabled and enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports are not set, so access to an internet-exposed database relies solely on a static shared password with no authentication or query audit trail for forensics.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = ON, so the publicly accessible database accepts unencrypted client connections; the bootstrapped PHP app uses mysqli_connect without TLS, sending master credentials and query data in cleartext.

user_data interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc in cleartext. User data is retrievable unauthenticated from the instance metadata service by any local process or SSRF vector, and is also stored in plaintext in Terraform state and visible in the EC2 console.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled on an instance running a public-facing PHP application. An SSRF flaw can retrieve both the plaintext user-data secrets and the instance profile credentials for the highly privileged ec2role.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the root volume — which persists the plaintext database credentials file — may be created unencrypted depending on the AMI and account default.
The bootstrap installs an HTTP-only Apache/PHP application that accepts and displays form-submitted personal data over port 80 with no TLS termination, transmitting application data in cleartext.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the instance profile of an internet-reachable web server. Theft of the instance credentials yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS databases in the account, including privilege escalation by launching instances with other roles.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, providing no outbound containment and easing data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.

The database endpoint is emitted as an unmarked (non-sensitive) output, publishing the reachable address of an internet-facing database to anyone with access to state files, CI logs, or terraform output.
